text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Paris Club to waive 4.2 million of Egypt's debt within days. Prime Minister Ganzouri tells reporters after opening the "Youth and Development" conference government spends nine billion pounds on subsidies for popular housing. Implementing the Mubarak Housing Project for youth in southern Egypt and plans for 190 new cities. The peace and development process Mubarak has led during the past 15 years has made Egypt a leader in the region. The agreement with the fund is a recognition for the state of the Egyptian economy.
- Mubarak receives a letter on the peace process from French President Jacques Chirac. The French leader will end a regional tour with a visit to Cairo.
- Al-Ahram, in front page editorial: Mubarak and another year in the grand process of giving.
- Cairo bourse turnover hits 7.3 billion pounds in the first 10 months of the year.
- Mubarak and Israel's Weizman discuss ways to push the peace process forward.

- Foreign Minister Moussa says after Mubarak met Chirac's envoy discussions focussed on the contributions of the European role in the peace process. The success of the peace process is linked to the Israeli position on issues of discord.
- A new natural gas discovery north of Port Said.
- Tunisian football team Safakis beats Zamalek in the semi-final of the African club competition. Ahli moves forward and beats Ittihad 2-0.
- A letter to Mubarak from Chirac on the European role in the peace process. Moussa says withdrawal from Hebron is not enough... all agreements must be implemented.
- Editor-in-Chief Mahfouz al-Ansari says in a front-page column: Especially to the president- may you be the first leader in Egypt to wipe out the illiteracy of the Egyptians. Mubarak is the future.
- Airforce head Ahmed Shafik says Egypt will buy the latest airplanes and weapons as needed.
- A conspiracy against Egypt. Ethiopia demands 16 billion cubic metres of Nile water and is supported by Israel and the World Bank.
